scenario.description: A finance director must approve and structure a proposed automated warehouse project, deciding the purchase method, capitalized amount, operating-expense allocation, tax election, and monitoring controls, with input from accounting control and tax.

shared_context.S1: The operations team proposes an automated warehouse project with a total vendor quote of $10,000,000.
shared_context.S2: The project is intended to improve order throughput at the company's main distribution center.
shared_context.S3: The vendor offers either an outright equipment purchase or a five-year equipment lease.
shared_context.S4: Elena makes the binding capital-allocation decision.
shared_context.S5: The finance team's normal project review includes a roundtable in which accounting control and tax report any issues before the approving officer settles the proposal.

PF1.text: Martin found while reviewing the vendor's invoice coding this week that $2,400,000 of the quote is implementation consulting and configuration support rather than equipment; it must be charged to operating expense, leaving exactly $7,600,000 eligible for capitalization, and he has not posted the correction to the project file yet.

PF2.text: Nadia received a tax memo this morning confirming that the qualifying automation equipment can receive the accelerated-depreciation election only if the company purchases and owns it rather than leases it; the memo has not yet been circulated to the capital-review file.

acceptance_conditions: The warehouse automation project must be approved.
The equipment must be purchased rather than leased.
Exactly $7,600,000 must be treated as capital expenditure.
Exactly $2,400,000 must be allocated to implementation operating expense.
The accelerated-depreciation election must be made.
The settlement must reflect the accounting split of $7,600,000 capital expenditure and $2,400,000 implementation operating expense.
The settlement must reflect that the accelerated-depreciation election is made.

decisive_facts.why: Without PF1, the full $10,000,000 quote would ordinarily be treated as capital expenditure; PF1 changes the capitalized amount to exactly $7,600,000 and the implementation expense to exactly $2,400,000.
Without PF2, the purchase-versus-lease choice and accelerated-depreciation election have no identified tax basis; PF2 changes the required funding choice to purchase and turns the election on.
